'''Radu I. Boț''' is a Romanian [[mathematician]] and an [[Academic staff|academic]]. He is a [[Professor]] as well as the Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Head of the Institute of Mathematics at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref name=ol>{{cite web|url=https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~rabot/cv.html|title=Radu Ioan Boţ - Curriculum Vitae}}</ref>

Boț's research focuces on convex analysis, convex optimization, nonsmooth optimization, and monotone operators.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazetanord-vest.ro/2026/01/excelenta-radu-ioan-bot-matematician-de-talie-mondiala-exemplu-de-performanta-academica-pentru-comunitatea-satmareana/|title=Colegiul Național „Mihai Eminescu” Satu Mare aduce în prim-plan un român de excepție, decan al Facultății de Matematică a Universității din Viena}}</ref> His works have been published in academic journals such as ''[[SIAM Journal on Optimization]]'', ''[[Mathematical Programming]]'', ''[[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]]'', ''[[Journal of Differential Equations]]'' and ''[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=hhmaYxQAAAAJ|title=Radu Ioan Bot - Google Scholar}}</ref>

==Education==
Boț completed his Diploma and [[Master of Science]] degrees in Mathematics from [[Babeș-Bolyai University]], Cluj-Napoca, in 1998 and 1999, respectively. He subsequently completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] at [[Chemnitz University of Technology]] in 2003. In 2008, he obtained his Habilitation (Dr. rer. nat. habil.), and the following year he was granted the title of Privatdozent (PD) by the same university.<ref name=ol/>

==Career==
Boț began his academic career at the Faculty of Mathematics of Chemnitz University of Technology, where he was from 2003 to 2010 and again from 2011 to 2013. From 2010 to 2011, he held a position as professor of [[applied mathematics]] at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf. Between 2014 and 2017, he was an associate professor in the Faculty of Mathematics at University of Vienna, where he has been professor of applied mathematics since 2017.<ref name=ol/>

In addition to his academic roles, Boț has undertaken several administrative appointments. He was Vice Dean for Research of the Faculty of Mathematics and Deputy Head of the Institute of Mathematics from 2016 to 2020. He also worked as the Speaker of the Vienna School of Mathematics at the University of Vienna. From 2020 to 2025, he was the Speaker of the ‘’Vienna Graduate School on Computational Optimization”, which was funded by the [[Austrian Science Fund]]. Since 2020, he has been Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Head of the Institute of Mathematics at the University of Vienna.<ref name=ol/>

Since 2026, Boț has served as [[editor-in-chief]] of the ''[[SIAM Journal on Optimization]]''.

==Research==
In his early research, Boț developed and compared various dual optimization problems using the Fenchel–Rockafellar approach for convex programs with inequality constraints, studied relations among them, and established strong duality and optimality conditions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wanka |first1=Gert |last2=Boţ |first2=Radu-Ioan |title=On the Relations Between Different Dual Problems in Convex Mathematical Programming |journal=Operations Research Proceedings 2001 |date=2002 |pages=255–262 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-50282-8_32 |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-50282-8_32 |publisher=Springer |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Subsequently, he extended Farkas’ Lemma to systems with finite and infinite convex constraints, using two duality frameworks: extended Fenchel and Fenchel–Lagrange duals, and showed strong duality results that unified and generalized classical [[convex optimization]] theory.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bot |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Wanka |first2=Gert |title=Farkas-Type Results With Conjugate Functions |journal=SIAM Journal on Optimization |date=January 2005 |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=540–554 |doi=10.1137/030602332 |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/030602332 |issn=1052-6234|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Together with Wanka, he introduced a weaker conjugate epigraph-based regularity condition that ensured Fenchel duality in infinite-dimensional optimization and was applied to the strong conical hull intersection property of convex sets.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boţ |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Wanka |first2=Gert |title=A weaker regularity condition for subdifferential calculus and Fenchel duality in infinite dimensional spaces |journal=Nonlinear Analysis: Theory, Methods & Applications |date=15 June 2006 |volume=64 |issue=12 |pages=2787–2804 |doi=10.1016/j.na.2005.09.017 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0362546X05008266 |issn=0362-546X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2009, he co-authored the book titled ''Duality in Vector Optimization'', wherein he focused on duality theory in vector optimization, filling a literature gap by providing a comprehensive research-oriented treatment intended for researchers and graduate students in mathematics and optimization.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/646816742|title=Duality in Vector Optimization}}</ref> In the subsequent year, he authored the book ''Conjugate Duality in Convex Optimization''. The book explored advanced convex optimization, focusing on conjugate duality, regularity conditions, biconjugate calculus, and Fenchel duality, while developing new duality frameworks and applying them to monotone operators for researchers and graduate students.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/567353779|title=Conjugate Duality in Convex Optimization}}</ref> He also proposed primal-dual splitting algorithms for solving inclusions involving mixtures of composite and parallel-sum type monotone operators, which rely on an inexact Douglas-Rachford method, and investigated their convergence properties.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boţ |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Hendrich |first2=Christopher |title=A Douglas--Rachford Type Primal-Dual Method for Solving Inclusions with Mixtures of Composite and Parallel-Sum Type Monotone Operators |journal=SIAM Journal on Optimization |date=January 2013 |volume=23 |issue=4 |pages=2541–2565 |doi=10.1137/120901106 |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/120901106 |issn=1052-6234|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In collaboration with Csetnek and Hendrich, Boț developed and analyzed an inertial Douglas–Rachford splitting algorithm for monotone inclusions, proved convergence, extended it to structured operators, and demonstrated applications to primal–dual convex optimization with numerical experiments in clustering and location theory.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boţ |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Csetnek |first2=Ernö Robert |last3=Hendrich |first3=Christopher |title=Inertial Douglas–Rachford splitting for monotone inclusion problems |journal=Applied Mathematics and Computation |date=1 April 2015 |volume=256 |pages=472–487 |doi=10.1016/j.amc.2015.01.017 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0096300315000314 |issn=0096-3003|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In collaboration with Nguyen, he introduced an inertial continuous-time model with an asymptotically vanishing term for minimizing continuously differentiable convex functions under linear equality constraints, proving fast convergence of the primal-dual gap, feasibility measure, and objective value, together with weak convergence of the trajectory to a primal-dual optimal solution.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boţ |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Nguyen |first2=Dang-Khoa |title=Improved convergence rates and trajectory convergence for primal-dual dynamical systems with vanishing damping |journal=Journal of Differential Equations |date=5 December 2021 |volume=303 |pages=369–406 |doi=10.1016/j.jde.2021.09.021 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022039621005799 |issn=0022-0396|arxiv=2106.12294 }}</ref> He also addressed minimax optimization in [[machine learning]], proving novel global convergence guarantees for stochastic alternating gradient descent ascent in challenging non-convex–non-concave settings, relevant to training GANs and adversarial models.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boţ |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Böhm |first2=Axel |title=Alternating Proximal-Gradient Steps for (Stochastic) Nonconvex-Concave Minimax Problems |journal=SIAM Journal on Optimization |date=30 September 2023 |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=1884–1913 |doi=10.1137/21M1465470 |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/21M1465470 |issn=1052-6234|url-access=subscription }}</ref> More recently, he introduced a Fast Optimistic Gradient Descent Ascent (OGDA) method, in both continuous and discrete time, establishing convergence of the generated trajectories and iterates while achieving the best-known convergence rates among schemes for solving monotone equations.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boţ |first1=Radu Ioan |last2=Csetnek |first2=Ernö Robert |last3=Nguyen |first3=Dang-Khoa |title=Fast Optimistic Gradient Descent Ascent (OGDA) Method in Continuous and Discrete Time |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |date=1 February 2025 |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=163–222 |doi=10.1007/s10208-023-09636-5 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10208-023-09636-5 |language=en |issn=1615-3383|doi-access=free }}</ref>
